events.label: birth
events.text: Daniel Cottier born in Glasgow, son of Margaret McLean and Daniel Cottier.

evidence.quote: Daniel Cottier was born in 1838

events.text: Recorded with his family in Carrick Street, Glasgow, in the census.

evidence.quote: In the Census of 1841 , he is recorded with his family in Carrick Street

events.text: Working as an apprentice coach painter, living in North Woodside Road, Glasgow.

evidence.quote: By 1851 , he was working as an apprentice coach painter

events.text: Went to London, possibly working for stained glass makers Ward & Hughes.

evidence.quote: Around 1859 he went to London

events.text: Boarding in Francis Street, St Pancras, London.

evidence.quote: In 1861 , he was boarding in Francis Street , St Pancras , London

events.text: Working as a glass designer in London.

evidence.quote: In 1861 , he was boarding in Francis Street , St Pancras , London , working as a glass designer

events.text: Returned to Scotland as manager of Field & Allan, slaters, glaziers and decorators.

evidence.quote: In 1862 Cottier returned to Scotland to accept an appointment as manager of Field & Allan

events.text: Oversaw glazing and decoration of Peddie and Kinnears Pilrig Parish Church, Leith.

evidence.quote: oversaw the glazing and decoration of Peddie and Kinnears Pilrig Parish Church , Leith ( c . 1862–63 )

events.label: founding
events.text: Opened his own business in Edinburgh, after two years managing Field & Allan.

evidence.quote: In 1862 Cottier returned to Scotland to accept an appointment as manager of Field & Allan
After managing Field & Allan for two years , Cottier felt sufficiently confident to open his own business in Edinburgh

events.text: Art furnishing business opened branches in Edinburgh, Glasgow and London (to 1869).

evidence.quote: His art furnishing business opened branches in Edinburgh , Glasgow and London between 1864 and 1869

events.text: Married Marion Millar Field in Edinburgh.

evidence.quote: In 1866 , he married Marion Millar Field
married Marion , the late William Fields daughter , in Edinburgh on 15 June 1866

events.label: award
events.text: Armorial window received a prize at the Paris International Exhibition.

evidence.quote: At the 1867 Paris International Exhibition , Cottiers armorial window received a prize
had recently won a prize for the superb harmony of colours in his armorial window at the 1867

events.text: Miriam and David stained glass window in the former Dowanhill Church, Glasgow.

evidence.quote: including Miriam and David ( 1867 )

events.text: Moved the centre of his activities to London.

evidence.quote: by the time he moved to London in 1869
in 1869 he moved the centre of his activities to London

events.label: founding
events.text: Established Cottier and Company at 2 Langham Place, London, as art furniture makers.

evidence.quote: Encouraged by his growing success , in 1869
in partnership with Brydon , Wallace and John Bennett , he established Cottier and Company

events.text: Small naturalistic stained glass windows made for Prudhoe Hall.

evidence.quote: Made around 1870 , they pre-date by ten years or more

events.text: Opened branches in New York, Sydney and Melbourne; Sydney branch run with John Lamb Lyon.

evidence.quote: in 1873 he opened more branches in New York , Sydney and Melbourne
In 1873 he opened a New York branch at 144 Fifth Avenue
In 1873 Cottier began to export the Aesthetic Movement to Australia with the opening of a branch in Sydney

events.text: Remained an active designer on several American projects until 1879.

evidence.quote: Cottier remained an active designer on several American project between 1873–9

events.text: Musician Angels window at St Machar's Cathedral, Aberdeen.

evidence.quote: the Musician Angels at St Machars Cathedral , Aberdeen ( 1873 )

events.text: Window made for the main hall of William Sherman's house in Newport, Rhode Island.

evidence.quote: An important window made in about 1877 for the main hall of the Newport , Rhode Island , house

events.text: Baptism of Christ window in Paisley Abbey.

evidence.quote: the Baptism of Christ in Paisley Abbey , Renfreshire ( c . 1880 )

events.label: death
events.text: Died of a heart attack aged 53 while visiting Jacksonville, Florida.

evidence.quote: Cottier died of a heart attack on April 15 , 1891

events.text: His New York firm ceased operating as picture dealers.

evidence.quote: His firm survived in New York as picture dealers until 1915

undated_mentions: apprenticeship at a Glasgow glazing and decorating firm (1850s)
collaboration with Louis Comfort Tiffany and John La Farge (1880s)
son Archibald died of whooping cough aged 20 months (date not stated)
